function: Predicts the beam coherence time (interval between beam updates) of a near-field THz link from UE position, speed, carrier frequency, and array size, to cut beam-update overhead (pp. 2-3).
system: THz link: AP with 512-antenna ULA, single-antenna mobile UE, spherical-wave near/far-field channel with L=2 scatterers, fc 142 GHz (also 280 GHz), 20 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (pp. 1, 3).
method: Feedforward network (6 fully connected layers) with 12-dimensional input (three mobility snapshots, fc, N); supervised offline training on labels from numerical T_B, smooth L1 loss (pp. 2-3).
data_channel: Own simulated dataset: spherical-wave channel, 2 scatterers, path gains from the close-in sub-THz path-loss model of [13], Gauss-Markov mobility; 2.5e5 samples split 80/10/10 (pp. 2-3).
test_conditions: Trained at fc 142 and 280 GHz; tested on 100 trajectories per mobility type at 142 GHz (Fig. 3) and at 180, 220 GHz (Fig. 5) (pp. 3-5).
baselines: Non-learned: statistical T_C updates, numerical T_B (exhaustive-search ground truth), ideal upper bound with perfect CSI and no overhead. No learned baseline; others omitted (p. 4).
metrics: Effective data rate over time (Fig. 3), average beam-update duration (Fig. 4), average effective rate versus carrier frequency (Fig. 5), and inference time per sample (pp. 3-5).
complexity: Measured average inference time 5.3 microseconds per sample versus about 2 s for the numerical T_B at N=512, 142 GHz; 6-layer feedforward network (pp. 2-3).
q1_support: p. 3: "using the close-in (CI) model in [13, Eq. (1)]" for the path gains, inside a custom spherical-wave simulator with Gauss-Markov mobility (p. 2); it is not 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "model is trained only for 142 and 280 GHz", yet Fig. 5 (p. 5) plots the effective rate at 142, 180, 220, and 280 GHz, so 180 and 220 GHz are carrier frequencies unseen in training; p. 3 also gives the training set as fc in {142, 280} GHz.
q3_support: p. 4: "we omit other baselines and limit the comparison to the exhaustive search method"; the benchmarks (upper bound, statistical TC, numerical TB) are all non-learned, and no earlier learned predictor or standard learning model is compared.
q4_support: p. 3: "the measured average inference time per sample is only 5.3" microseconds; p. 2: the numerical approach, "it takes on average 2 seconds" for N = 512 and fc = 142 GHz.
q5_support: p. 1: "relies on relevant simulated data"; the dataset is self-generated (p. 3), no code or data link is given, and no public or measured dataset is used.
notes: Area 3 is borderline: the network outputs the beam coherence time, that is, how long a beam stays valid, while the beam vector itself is computed from the UE position (p. 4). I treat beam-update control as beam management (area 3), not channel prediction (area 2) or link adaptation; the reviewer should confirm. q1 is 0: the close-in sub-THz path-loss model of [13] sits inside a custom simulator and the data are simulated, not measured. q2 is 1 from the training statement on p. 3 and p. 5 and the markers of Fig. 5, which I read from the page image (points at 142, 180, 220, 280 GHz). q3 is 0: no learned baseline; RNN and LSTM are only mentioned as not used (p. 3).
